Recommendations of sixth World Hindi Conference 
†*401. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN SINGH: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the recommendation of the Sixth World Hindi Conference organised 
in London; 
(b) whether these recommendations have been implemented fully, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) What would be the terms of reference of the next conference? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH): (a) to  (d) A statement is laid on the 
table of the House. 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

[10 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
Statement 
(a) to (d) The VI World Hindi Conf erence was organised at London 
from 14th to 18th September, 1999. The major recommendations of the 
Conference included, that Mahatma Gandhi International Hindi University 
should be developed as an international centre of Hindi learning. The 
Governments of India and Mauritius should expedite the process of 
establishment of World Hindi Secretaria t in Mauritius. Serious efforts should 
be made towards recognition of Hindi as one of the official languages in the 
UN. Our Missions/Posts should liaise with the people of Indian origin so that 
teaching of Hindi is promoted in the countries of their accreditation and Hindi 
books and other teaching material should  be provided to them as required. 
Hindi learning should be facilitated with the use of the advancement of 
information technology. 
The Government made every effort to implement the recommendations. 
The Mahatma Gandhi International Hindi University has been established and 
is functioning as an international centre of Hindi tearing. After a 
Memorandum of Understanding having been signed between India and 
Mauritius, the Mauritian National Assembly has passed a Bill on 16th 
November, 2002 for setting up of the Secretariat. A high-level Committee has 
also been set up under the chairmanship  of External Affairs. Minister on the 
subject of recognising Hindi as one of the Official Languages in the UN. Our 
Missions/Posts are maintaining close liaison with the Hindi scholars/ 
organisations in the countries of their accreditation with a view to support and 
enrich their Hindi propagating activities. Hindi learning material, books, CDs, 
software are being catered to them by  the Ministry, as per their demands. 
Different software to facilitate Hind i teaching have been developed by C-
DAC, Pune, such as, LILA PRABODH and PRAVEEN and these are also 
being used for Hindi learning. 
The VII World Hindi Conference is being organised at Paramaribo 
(Surinam) from 5th to 9th June, 2003. "World Hindi - Challenges of the new 
Century" is the theme of the VII World Hindi Conference. Emphasis will be 
on exploring the ways and means of popularising the use of Hindi among 
foreigners, particularly people of Indian origin, facilitating the learning of 
Hindi using modem methods and

rich legacy of Hindi language and literature.

restrictions on procurement of services by the State.

these bills deal with only state go vernment contracts which account for a 
fraction of business of Indian call centres. 
(c) and (d) With active support from the Government of India,

legislators, customers and US Industry Associations to highlight the benefits 
of outsourcing, creation of jobs and competitiveness of various industries. A 
NASSCOM delegation visited USA in March 2003 and had meetings at New 
Jersey, Washington D.C., Maryland and Washington. It has also hired a 
reputed Public Relations firm to do the lobbying on behalf of the Indian IT 
Industry.

Slashing of rates by cellular companies 
*407.  SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: 
SHRI RAJU PARMAR: 
Will the Minister of COMMU NICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that cellular companies in the country have 
slashed their rates for mobile users; 
(b) if so, what are the rates/schemes at present being offered by these 
cell phone operators; and 
(c) whether the rates of MTNI and BSNL are very high as compared 
to the cell phone operators, and if so , the comparative rates of cell phone 
operators vis-a-vis the landline operators namely MTNL/BSNL/VSNL? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House. 
19 

RAJYA  SABHA [10 April, 2003] 
Statement 
(a) and (b) Sir, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is 
responsible for fixation of tariffs fo r telecom services including Cellular 
Mobile Telephone Service (CMTS) in the country. Tariff for CMTS is 
currently under forbearance which mean s that the cellular operators are at 
liberty to offer various tariff options. Tariffs for CMTS have shown a 
continuously downward tren d in the recent past; this  is mainly due to the 
increased competition in the Cellular Sector. Cellular operators have various 
tariff plans with varying rates of monthly rental and airtime charges, which 
they go on revising from time to time. Information provided by TRAI 
indicates that currently there are more th an 600 different tariff plans available 
for the cellular subscribers across the country. 
(c) No, Sir. The rates of MTNL and BSNL are comparable and quite 
competitive as compared to the other operators. However, in view of the large 
number of different tariff plans across the country, it is not possible to make a 
meaningful comparison between the tari ffs charged for CMTS by the cellular 
operators and those charged by BSNL and MTNL for land line phones (under 
Basic Telephone Sen/ices). VSNL does not operate CMTS or Basic 
Telephone Service. 
SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: Sir, the private cell operators are 
charging from Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 7,5000, as advance deposit, from subscribers 
for providing STD and ISD facilities. This is unjustified as crores of rupees 
are collected by cell operat ors for providing this service. In most of the 
advanced countries this practice is not adhered to. I would like to know from 
the hon. Minister whether he would di rect the TRAI to examine it and take 
positive actions in the interest of the consumers. 
SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, whethe r there will be large or small 
downpayments to be charged by the operator, it is to be determined 
completely by the market. In the TRAI's order on which there was a full 
discussion last time, in- the first half of the Session, as you know, they have 
given forbearance, that is, whatever am ount the persons want to charge, the 
operators want to charge and the cons umers are willing to pay, the cellular 
operators have that freedom in this regard. 
Now, I come to the issue of the consumers getting, agitated on this 
matter. Sir, they will walk away from the competition and go to 
20 

[10 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
some other provider - especially, I will be happy if they come to BSNL. But 
the more important point is that there is a procedure -laid down in the Act 
passed by the Parliament - which prescribes that if there is a group of 
consumers agitated about a particular method or aggrieved about a particular 
method, they can go to TDSAT for redressal. But if it is an individual 
consumer, he can go to the consumer  bodies set up under the Consumer 
Protection Act, 1988. 
SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: Sir, my second supplementary is: 
Although the Government is committed to provide excellent service to 
consumers, recently, it has been noticed  that due to corporate rivalry,

operators, MTNL and BSNL to resolve all the pending issues of

SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, that is absolutely right. But it is corporate 
rivalry which has brought the rates down from Rs. 16.80 per minute to Rs. 
1.80 per minute. It is because of corporate rivalry. 
I come to the question of interconnectivity. You are right that in 
January this year, there was a problem. But as far as I know, there is no 
problem at the moment. That episode wh en they were not connecting calls of 
each other's networks is a matter that is now before TDSAT. TRAI itself has 
sent notices to all these people to explai n as to what happened at that time. 
But, if there is a specific complaint about interconnectivity, I would be 
delighted to look into it. 
SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Sir, the private cell phone operators have 
reduced the tariff and call charges dr astically during the last one year, 
although the cost of maintenance has remained unchanged. I would like to 
ask the hon. Minister the reasons for in creasing the rental and call charges as 
well as for reducing the pulse rate by MTNL and BSNL during the last one 
year. 
SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, as you kn ow, in the TRAI's order, it was 
prescribed that the rentals should be  increased. As I explained last time, 
BSNL and MTNL have given alternate packages to TRAI. 
21 

RAJYA SABHA [10 April, 2003] 
Due to the TRAI regulations. I am not in a position to disclose those 
packages, but you will find that the concerns expressed in this House by 
Members, both on monthly rentals and on pulse rates, have been addressed in 
those packages. If TRAI approves those packages, you will be very much 
satisfied with the result. Of course, this also means that the surplus of BSNL 
will be drastically reduced, because they used to finance the roll out to village 
telephony all by charging more on long distance telephony and those rates 
have collapsed as Mr. Parmar himself mentioned. If they do not increase 
rentals, they will have less surplus to roll out telephone services to the 
villages and for other things and then you will complain about it. 
In the next four years, BSNL requir es Rs. 29,000 crores for rolling out 
obligations. In the Five Year Plan, they have been given a princely sum. of 
Rs. 1 crore per year! That means for the four years, only Rs. 4 crores. So, we 
have to raise money from one place or the other. 
SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Sir, when  the private cell operators come 
out with advertisements, they quote one rate and at the time of billing, they 
charge different rates. What steps is the TRAI going to take to ensure that the

SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, as I have explained in my answer, there 
are 600 different packages in  the market that are available to the subscribers. 
There are 600 different types of rate arrangements. So, a consumer may be

package. If there is any specific comp laint which the service provider does 
not attend to, as I have explained to you, it is either the Consumer Court 
which will look into it or if there is a group of consumers that is aggrieved, it 
will be taken care of by the TDSAT.

Conduct of WLL Players 
*415. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATION 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be p.eased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that as per Cellular Operators Association of 
India, WLL companies are misleading the public; 
(b) if so, whether the COAI has urged Government and TRAI to check 
role of the players of WLL who are cheating the public; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the concrete plans formulated to check the role of the WLL 
players? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (d) Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) had 
complained to Government and Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
(TRAI) that one basic service operator is indulging in mis-informing public 
by giving full page advertisements in national dailies proclaiming that they 
will be offering free all India roaming. Also that another basic service 
operator is providing limited mobilit y facility beyond its licensed service 
area of Delhi. 
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) sought comments of M/s. 
Tata Teleservices Ltd. and M/s. Reliance Infocom Ltd. TRAI has thereafter 
noted that M/s. Tata Teleservices Ltd. are making efforts to control the radio 
frequency spillage beyond Delhi Short Distance Charging Area (SDCA) and they 
will be constantly monitoring the situation to control and minimize the radio 
frequency spillage. TRAI has further emphasized that M/s. Tata Teleservices 
should offer WLL (MOBILE) service within the SDCA area. M/s. Reliance 
Infocom Ltd. responded by stating that they have stopped advertisments 
referring to roaming services. 
A meeting was held by the Government with the basic service 
operators and cellular mobile service operators in New Delhi on 14.2.2003. 
In the meeting, M/s. Reliance Infocom Ltd. informed that  the advertisement 
referring to roaming service will be withdrawn. Since then, no such 
advertisment has been reported.

Service operators to ensure service pr ovision within their service area in 
accordance with their respective licence conditions.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN): (a) and (b) Sir, Fault rate in Delhi unit 
of MTNL is slightly on the higher side. The average fault rate per hundred per 
month in Delhi unit for the year 2002-03 (upto 31-01-2003) is 19.99, as 
against average of all Indian fault rate of 11.00 for the same period. 
Not only the Telecom network of Delhi is one of the oldest where paper 
core underground cables still exists but due to very fast development of basic 
infrastructure like construction of flyovers, widening of roads, digging by 
other utility services to maintain and meet growing demand of fast expanding 
population, there are more damages to  underground cables. However, the 
fault rate for the month of February, 2003 has been brought down to 17.27 
faults per 100 subscribers per month. 
(c) The steps taken to improve the telephone services of MTNL are 
given in the enclosed statement. 
Statement 
Steps taken to improve the telephone services of MTNL 
MTNL, Delhi has initiated several measures to reduce the fault rate as 
listed below: 
1. All the electro mechanical exchanges and analog electronic 
exchanges in MTNL, Delhi have be en replaced by digital electronic 
exchanges. 
86 

[10 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
2. Paper core underground cables ar e being replaced by Jelly filled 
cables/Optical fibre cables with Digital Loop Carriers (D.L.Cs.)- 
3. For higher capacity primary cables and junction cables, duct 
systems has been introduced. 
4. Rehabilitation work in respect of leading in cables and rewiring of 
multi storeyed building is being done. 
5. Overhead wires are minimized by introducing 5 pair cables and wall 
Distribution Points (DPs). 
6. The junction network has been completely transferred to optical 
fibre cable links. 
7. Further improvement is being done by providing Synchronous 
Digital Hierarchy (SDH) systems connected on the ring architecture. 
8. Subscriber loop length being reduced by planning more 
Remote Subscriber Units (RSUs)/R emote Line Units (RLUs)/Digital 
Loop Carriers (DLCs). 
9. Wireless technologies like Cordect, Wireless in Local Loop 
(WLL) have been introduced. Faults are monitored on daily basis by 
senior officers. 
10. Computerised fault reporting system is introduced, which helps in 
booking, testing and sending the faults to the concerned line staff. 
11. In addition to this, line staff is provided with pagers for easy 
communication and follow up with the testing staff for speedy clearance of 
faults. 
12. Managed leased Data Network system has been introduced to 
improve the performance of the leased circuits. 
13. MTNL has liberalized the policy to replace all telephone 
instruments older than 5 years or repaired more than 2 times. This is being 
implemented in phases. In the first phase, instruments more than eight years 
old are being replaced.

Statement 
Steps taken by the Government to promote the Information Technology 
Sector 
1. Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG) has been 
rationalized and extended uniformly to all sectors without any 
threshold limit on payment of 5% duty. 
2. Approvals for all foreign direct investment proposals relating to the 
Information Technology sector, wi th the exception of Business-to-
Consumer (B2C) e-commerce are under the automatic route. 
3. Electronics Hardware Technology  Park (EHTP) and software 
Technology Park (STP) schemes are implemented under the aegis of the 
Department of Information Technology, Ministry of Communications 
and Information Technology, through a single window mechanism of 
the Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee (IMSC). 
4. Supplies of Information Technology Agreement (ITA-1) items in the 
Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) by EHTP/EOU/EPZ units shall be 
counted towards fulfillment of minimum Net Foreign Exchange 
earning as a Percentage of exports (NFEP) and the minimum Export 
Performance (EP), provided that the items are manufactured in the unit and 
attract zero rate of basic customs duty. Positive NFEP is required to be 
achieved in 5 years instead of every year. 
5. DTA access upto 50% of the FOB value of export is permitted for 
electronics hardware units under EOU/EPZ/EHTP schemes and the 
software units under EOU/EPZ/STP schemes. 
6. Accelerated depreciation norms extended to computers and computer 
peripherals to all units and capital goods of IT hardware units under 
Export Oriented schemes (EOU/ EPZ/EHTP). These shall stand 
depreciated to overall limit of 90% over a period of 3 years. 
107 

RAJYA  SABHA [10 April, 2003] 
7. Special Economic Zones are being set up to enable hassle free 
manufacturing and trading for export purposes. 
8. The Depreciation on Computers is allowed @ 60%. 
9. In the Budget 2002-03, the peak rate of customs duty has been reduced 
from 35% to 30%. Customs duty has been reduced on stepper motors 
for computers/printers from 5% to 0%, floppy diskette and unrecorded 
magnetic tape from 15% to 10%, ink cartridges/ribbon 
assembly/ribbon gear assembly/ribbon gear carriage for use in printers 
for computers from 25% to 5%, 56 items of capital goods for 
manufacture of semiconductors form 5% to 0%, 24 items of capital 
goods for manufacture of electronic components from 25-35% to 15%, 
tools/moulds/dies for electronics industry from 25% to 15% and on 46 
items of raw materials for manufacture of electronic components from 
25-35% to 5%. 
* Customs duty on Computers and Peripherals continues to be @15% 
and all storage devices, integrated circuits, microprocessors, data 
display tubes and deflection components of colour monitors 
continue at 0%. The concessional rate of customs duty @5% for 
specified raw materials for the electronics industry (121 items) 
continues. Customs duty on Information Technology Agreement 
(ITA-1) items of WTO (IT and Telecom products) continues @15%, 
parts of Telecom continue @5%, parts, components and accessories of 
mobile handsets including cellular telephones continue at 0%. 
10. The Central Excise duty structure was rationalized form multiple rates 
to single rate of 16% and single rate of Special Excise Duty (SED) @ 
16%, in the Budget 2001 -02, and continues. 
11. Information Technology Software is exempted from Customs and 
Excise Duty. 
 
12. Second hand capital goods upto 10 years are freely importable. 
13. EOU/EPZ/STP/EHTP units are eligible for Income Tax benefit on 
export profits, upto 2010, in terms of Sections 10A and 10B of the 
Income Tax Act. 
14. Exemption of withholding tax on interest on External Commercial 
Borrowings (ECBs) is available to the IT sector. 
108 

[10 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
15. Definition of Computer Software, as in Section 80 HHE of the Income Tax 
Act covers transmission of data. 
16. Benefit of Section 80 HHE is available to supporting software 
developers. 
17. IT Enabled Services are eligible for Income Tax benefit under 
Sections 10A, 10B and 80HHE of the Income Tax Act. 
18. DEPB rate will be same for a product whether exported as CBU or in 
CKD/SKD condition. 
19. Threshold limit for obtaining "Export House" status reduced to Rs. 5 
crores from Rs. 15 crores for Small Scale Industry, tiny sector, cottage 
sector, units located in North Ea st States/Sikkim/ J and K, and 
exporters exporting to countries in Latin America/ CIS/Sub Sahara 
Africa and units having ISO 9000 (Series) status. The status holders are 
eligible for the following new/special facilities: 
*100% retention of foreign exchange in Exchange Earners' 
Foreign Currency (EEFC) account; 
* Enhancement in normal repatriation period from 180 days to 360 
days. 
20. The donation of computers, imported duty free by EOU/EPZ/STP/ EHTP 
units to recognized non-commercial educational institutions, registered 
charitable hospitals, public libraries, public funded research and 
development establishments, etc., two years after their use by the said 
units is permitted. 
21. The second-hand computers and computer peripherals donated by an 
outside donor to Government schools and recognized schools run on a 
non-commercial basis by any organization are exempted from customs 
duties. 
22. Income by way of dividends or long-term capital gains of a Venture 
Capital Fund or Venture Capital company from investment made by 
way of equity shares in a Venture Capital Undertakings, which 
has been expanded to include the Software and IT sectors, will 
henceforth not be included in computing the total income. 
109 

RAJYA  SABHA [10 April, 2003] 
23. To give thrust to Venture Capital Finance, SEBI has been made the 
single point nodal agency for registration and regulation of both domestic 
and overseas venture capital funds. 
24. There will be no tax on distributed or undistributed income of Venture 
Capital Funds. The income distributed by the VCFs will only be taxed 
in the hands of the investors at the rates applicable to the nature of the 
income. VCFs will continue to be eligible for exemption even if the shares 
of the VC undertaking in which the VCFs have made the in itial 
investment are subsequently listed in a recognized stock exchange in 
India. 
25. Under policy on portfolio investment, Foreign Institutional Investors (Flls) 
are permitted to invest in a comp any upto an aggregate of 24% of 
equity shares, extendable upto 40% subject to approvals. This limit was 
raised from 40% to 49% in the Budget 2001 -02. 
26. Tax holiday under provisions of Section 80-IA (Infrastructure Status) has 
been extended to Internet Serv ice Providers (ISPs) and Broadband 
Network providers. 
27. Two-way fungibility has been permitted for ADRs/GDRs. Local shares can 
be reconverted into ADRs/GDRs, subject to sectoral caps. 
28. With a view to give a boost to the manufacturing sector, it is proposed 
in the Budget announcements 2002-03, to allow a deduction of a 
further sum of 15% of the actual cost of such machinery or plant 
acquired and installed after 31.3.2002 in case of new industrial 
undertaking or substantial expansion by an existing industrial 
undertaking. The proposed amendment will take effect from 1.4.2003 and 
will, accordingly, apply in relation to the assessment year 2003-04 and 
subsequent years. 
29. To encourage re-location of industries to India, plant and machineries 
would be permitted to be importe d without a licence, where the 
depreciated value of such relocating plants exceeds Rs. 50 crores. 
30. Indian Companies wishing to invest abroad may now invest upto US$ 
100 million on an annual basis through automatic route without being 
subject to the three year profitability condition, up from existing limit of 
US$ 50 million (Budget announcement 2002-03).

by market purchases may now do so without prior approval upto 50% of

32. To induce more investment for R&D activities, a weighted deduction of 
125% on the sums paid to any university, college or an institution or a

33. For reduction of transaction time for export/import clearances,

AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SUBHASH 
MAHARIA): (a) and (b) No, Sir. The total stocks of foodgrains available in the 
Central Pool as on 1st March 2003, was 36.19 million tonnes. Out of this stock, 
the Food Corporation of India (FCI) is holding 19.93 million tonnes stocks of 
foodgrains against the total storage capacity of 32.39 million tonnes all over the 
country. Thus, at present, the FCI is having vacant storage space of 12.46 
million tones (as on 28.2.2003). Foodgrains are stored in a scientific manner in 
the FCI godowns and regular prophylactic and curative treatments are carried out 
for the preservation of the foodgrains. 
(c). During the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007), the FCI has 
proposed to construct its own storage capacity of 6.42 lakh MTs all 
140 

[10 April, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
over the country to meet future demand and supply. Out of this a storage 
capacity of 0.79 lakh MTs has been realised upto February 2003. Besides, 
Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) and State Warehousing Corporations 
(SWCs) have also created storage cap acity of about 6 million tonnes under 
seven years guarantee scheme in the main procuring States. 
The following steps havebeen taken by the Government of India to utilize 
the foodgrains over and above the buffer norms: 
(i) The allocation of foodgrains has been increased from 25 Kgs to 35 
Kgs per family per month for the consumers under Targeted 
Public Distribution System (TPDS). 
(ii) The sale of foodgrains (Wheat and Rice) would be continued under 
Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) without quantitative restrictions 
at the prices to be determined by the High Level Committee of 
the FCI upto 31.3.2004. 
(iii) The export of rice, wheat and wheat products would be continued 
till 31.3.2004 without quantitative restrictions subject to the 
condition that the stocks in Central Pool will not be lower than the 
buffer stock of 243 lakh MTs (100 lakh MT rice and 143 lakh MT 
wheat) 
(iv) The foodgrains are being issued under various welfare schemes 
like Mid-day-Meal scheme etc. at BPL rates instead of economic 
prices. 
(v) Wheat and rice being issued @ Rs. 2 & Rs. 3/Kg. respectively to the 
"poorest of the poor" families under the Anotodaya Anna Yojana 
(AAY). 
(vi) Additional allocation of foodgrains have been made on "free of 
cost" basis under the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) 
and the special component of the SGRY

SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:

(a) whether Government have received any suggestions to

completely transform the Food Corporation of India with a view to reducing the 
expenditure of the corporation; 
(b) if so, when and where from Government have received the same; and 
(c) the details of the suggestions and the extent to which reduction in 
expenditure is estimated to be achieved as a result thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI V. SREENIVASA 
PRASAD): (a) and (b)The Administrative Staff College of India (Hyderabad), in its 
Report submitted in May 2001, has, inter-alia, suggested that the Government 
and the FCI should consider policy changes and other measures to restructure 
the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to reduce the expenditure of the 
corporation. 
(c) The major recommendations in the Report with regard to the 
restructuring of the FCI are that the Government and the FCI should consider 
the 'unbunding' of the FCI operations, either functionally or spatially. This 
could be achieved either by dividing FCI operations by handing over 
procurement to State Governments, distribution to the railways and physical 
verification and storage to the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC). An 
alternative suggested is to create State level Corporation to carry out all the 
operations within the State. The Union level FCI would limit its procurement, 
storage etc. to the maintenance of the buffer stocks. The expected reduction of 
expenditure, on account of the proposed restructuring, has not been quantified 
in the Report.

damage and capture of their equipments and boats as reported in the press

northern waters by Sri Lankan fishermen during the civil war, Indian fishing 
vessels found it feasible to fish in Sri Lankan waters. With the coming into 
effect of the Cease-fire Agreement, ba n on Sri Lankan fishermen fishing in 
northern waters has been lifted.The Sri Lankan position is that the presence of 
Indian boats far within the Sri Lankan side of the IMBL, on a regular basis, 
cannot be termed accidental straying.

straying into Sri Lankan waters is known, the High Commission of India in

problem of our fishermen straying into Sri Lankan including (i) publicity against

Child labour in silk industry 
3042. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of 
LABOUR be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that an N.G.O. namely Human Rights Watch' 
has in a report stated that thousands of children toil hard as virtual slaves in 
country's silk industry; and 
(b) what new steps Government are ta king to eliminate the curse of 
child labour in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR 
(SHRI VIJAY GOEL): (a) Yes.Sir. 
(b) Government of India has taken steps for withdrawal and 
rehabilitation of child labour working in hazardous occupations to reduce the 
incidence of child labour in a particular district through the Schemes of 
National Child Labour Projects (N CLPs) and Grant-in-aid to Non-
Governmental Organisations/Voluntary Organisations. Under the Scheme, special 
schools have been set up in the child labour endemic districts with the 
provision for non-formal/formal education, vocational training, stipend, 
nutrition, health-care etc. So far, 100 NCLPs have been sanctioned in 13 child 
labour endemic States for coverage of 2.11 lakh children. 
In the Tenth Plan, the Government proposes to implement the Policy and 
programmes for elimination of child labour in a more focused, integrated and 
convergent manner. The Government would be making attempts to eliminate 
child labour from hazardo us occupations and progressively move towards 
elimination of child labour in all its forms in the coming year.

3057. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted a National Commission on

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) Yes, Sir.

11th May, 2000. It is headed by the Prime Minister as Chairman and the

Commission. The Terms of Reference of the Commission are given below:

the National Population Policy with a view to meeting the 
goals set out in the Policy.

environmental and developmental programmes so as to hasten 
population stabilization. 
(iii) To promote inter-sectoral coordination in planning and 
implementation across Government agencies of the Central and 
State Governments, to involve th e civil society and the private 
sector and to explore the possibilities of international 
cooperation in support of the goals set out in the Policy.

in support of this national effort.

Population to help the process of population stabilization in the country, a 
few are indicated below: 
• Recognizing that development and demography have a close 
inter-relationship, an immediate effort was made to bring 
together all the relevant Ministries/Departments and a Strategic 
Support Group of Secretaries of the concerned Departments was 
created on the basis of whose recommendations several 
Working/Advisory Groups/Task Forces were constituted by the 
NCP and concept papers prepared by several Ministries bringing 
out how they could reorient their programmes to address 
demographic concerns also. The reports/recommendations of 
these Groups were forwarded to the concerned Departments/ 
Divisions of the Planning Commission for being incorporated 
in the sectoral programmes of the Tenth Five Year Plan. 
• Regular review of the impact of the Family Welfare 
programmes in the high fertility States and the growth rate vis-a-
vis national level. 
• Identification of 133 districts having TFR > 3.5 for focussed 
action for population stabilization followed by a Conference of 
DMs of these districts to discuss and decide about various matters 
relating to population stabilization. 
• Selection of social, economic and demographic indicators for 
monitoring purpose and mapping and ranking of 569 districts 
of the country on the basis of 12 such indicators with a view to 
know the position of each district in relation to them. 
• To enable better integration of research related findings for 
policy formulation two Conferences of demographic research 
organizations were convened. 
• To understand the actual impact of the national family welfare 
programmes several field visits in the high fertility

areas were made so that the findings could be made use of for

ongoing social sector programmes and better utilization of the

Statement 
Problem being faced in implementing Golden Quadrilateral Project 
(i) Land Acquisition: 
Various legal/procedural requirements which are required to be 
completed before acquisition of land are delaying the progress. There are 
large number of structures, removal of which is also a time taking exercise. 
(ii) Removal of utilities: 
To enable the contractors to take up construction of the road, the land 
has to be made free of all encumbrances including utilities like water 
pipelines, electric poles, etc. Shifting of such utilities can be taken up only 
after the land is acquired, cleared of structures and made available to the 
contractor. 
(iii) Environmental/Forest clearance: 
Environmental clearance (including fo rest clearance in respect of land 
recorded as forest) has to be obtained. Many of the stretches also have trees 
and obtaining permission for cutting of trees is also a time taking exercise. 
(iv) Quarries: 
Contractors are finding it difficult in some States to obtain, permission 
for quarrying for aggregates and this also delaying the progress of work in 
some packages. 
(v) Law and Order: 
Law and order problems created by  anti-social elements are also 
hindering the work in some States. In some places the local people are 
preventing the construction work demanding charge of

acquired.

up by Minister for Road Transport and Highways with the concerned Chief 
Ministers to resolve the problems.

3076. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:  Will the Minister of ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the National Highways Authority of India has 
not stopped trucks and vehicles from carrying loose iron rods without proper 
safety measures; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) what steps would be taken to restrict movement of the dangerious loaded 
lorries and trucks on the National Highways; and 
(d) by when such restrictions would be imposed? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS MAJOR GENERAL (RETD.) (B.C. 
KHANDURI): (a) to (d) Vehicular movement on roads is governed by the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989. Section 
115 of the MV Act gives powers to the State Governments to restrict the use of 
vehicles, which affect public safety or convenience. The Section 190 of MV

hazardous nature to human life. Unde r Rule 93 of CMV Rules, the overall

provisions of MV Act and CMV Rules is  done by the respective States/UTs. 
National Highways Authority of India have no authority to check the 
movement of vehicles which affect public safety or convenience.

Credit flow to SSIs 
3084. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR: Will the Minister of SMALL 
SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the public sector banks have declined the request of his 
Ministry for access by SSI units to a fixed portion of priority sector lending; 
(b) whether an alternate suggestion wa s put forth to the public sector 
banks atleast to effect an increase of 10 per cent every year in lending to SSI 
units; 
(c) whether credit flow ot SSI units as percentage of net bank credit 
has decreased from 15.6 per cent in 1999 to 11.2 per cent during April-
September 2002; and 
(d) if so, the proposal mooted by Go vernment to increase the credit 
flow to SSI sector? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL 
SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) and (b) Considering 
the concerns regarding the declining trend of the percentage of SSI advacnes 
to Net bank Credit of Public Sector Banks, the Planning Commission 
convened a meeting on 10th December, 2002 under the Chairmanship of the 
Deputy Chairman to discuss various issues relating credit flow to SSI sector. 
As a follow up, the meeting of the Re serve Bank of India (RBI)'s Standing 
Advisory Committee on Flow of Institutional Credit to SSI sector was held 
on 15th January, 2003 in which the issue of fixing of a sub-target for the SSI 
sector within the priority sector was also discussed. It emerged that fixing a 
definite sub-target for SSI sector would have the effect of crowding out the 
residual sectors within the priority sector. Based on the decisions taken in 
this meeting, the RBI has advised the banks to consider budgeting their 
growth in advances to SSI sector keeping in view the trends in growth of net 
bank credit less food credit. 
(c) As per the information received from the RBI, while the quantum 
of credit flow to the SSI sector has gone up over the years, the percentage of 
total SSI advances to Net Bank credit has come down. The percentage of SSI 
advances to Net bank credit has decreased from 15.6 per cent as at the end of 
March, 2000 to 12.5 per cent as at the end of March, 2002. 
233

SSI include enhancement of working capital limit computed on the basis of 
minimum of 20% of annual projected turnover from Rs. 4 crore to Rs. 5 crore, 
enhancement in composite loan limit from Rs. 10 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs, raising 
of project cost limit under National Equity Fund Scheme from Rs. 25 lakhs to 
Rs. 50 lakhs, revision in eligible loan limit for coverage under. Credit 
Gurantee Scheme from Rs. 10 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs etc. Further, in accordance 
with the announcement made in the Union Budget 2003-04, the Indian Banks' 
Association has advised all its member banks to adopt an interest rate band of 
2 per cent above and below Prime Lending Rate (PLR) as announced by the 
State Bank of India.

(c) The steps taken to ensure control over cost overrun in projects and 
reduce delays include:

of project reports before investment approval; 
(ii) taking up of projects for implementation only after funds have 
been fully tied up; 
(iii) in-depth review of projects on monthly as well as quarterly basis 
by the Government; 
(iv) setting up of an Empowered Committee in the administrative 
Ministries for review of departmentally executed projects; 
(v) setting up of Standing Committees in the Ministries/ 
Departments to fix responsibility for time and cost overruns; 
(vi) appointment of nodal officers for each project with continuity of 
tenure; and 
(vii) issue of guidelines on standard bidding documents for 
adoption. 
These measures are expected to help minimise further cost overruns.

SPECIAL MENTIONS 
Need for provision of safe motherhood for all women of India 
SHRIMATI SHABANA AZMI (Nominated) : Madam, it is a crime and 
shame that five decades after Independenc e, we still have not been able to 
provide safe motherhood for our women. Tomorrow, on Kasturba Gandhi's 
birthday, we are going to celebrate Janani Suraksha Divas, and it is with 
regard to this that my Special Mention is on the provision of safe motherhood 
for all women of India as we celebrate Janani Suraksha Divas. 
Every year, over one lakh women in India die of complications 
related to pregnancy and childbirth. This would be equivalent to two Airbuses 
crashing every day. The majority of these women are from the most 
vulnerable strata of our society, poor and marginalised, tribal and scheduled 
castes. It is a shame that fifty years after Independence, one woman is still 
dying every five minutes from maternity complications. When a mother dies, 
her baby has six to ten times greater ch ance of dying as well. The majority of 
these deaths are preventable. Women in rural areas and urban slums need 
access to basic and emergency medical care during pregnancy, childbirth and 
post-partum period. Every pregnancy face s risk. Families and countries need 
a Birth Preparedness Plan. This requires specially skilled health personnel in 
rural areas, transportation to reach hospital, and 24 hour emergency services 
to manage complications, including blood transfusions. Health personnel 
including ANMs need to be trained in life saving skills to be able to 
appropriately respond to emergencies. It is a sorry state of affairs that health is 
not given the priority it deserves in our  country. Strong intervention is required 
from the Centre to ensure that Stat es with low health indices receive 
appropriate financial allocations. As we celebrate Janani Suraksha Divas, I 
would urge the Government to treat safe motherhood as not just a health 
issue but as a fundamental human right and commit itself to reducing deaths 
in childbirth within a fixed time frame.

Need for providing waterways transport facility between Chennai and 
Kanyakumari 
SHRI R. KAMARAJ (Tamil Nadu): Madam, I wish to draw the 
attention of the Government to the urgent need to develop waterways between 
Chennai and Kanyakumari to meet the heavy demand of passenger and 
goods traffic in the region. Since there is increasing traffic congestion on the 
road and rail traffic, the Government has to exploit the possibilities of inland 
waterways traffic. For travelling a distance of 703 kms between Chennai and 
Kanyakumari by road or rail, it takes about 15 hours. If waterways transport is 
used this distance can be reached in about 8 hours. Such a scheme will save 
fuel and time, and fare will be affordable even by a common man. Along the 
East Coast, between Chennai and Kanyakum ari, there are famous places like 
Mamallapuram, Pondicherry, Chidambaram, Pichavaram, Poombukar, 
Nagore, Vellankanni, Kodiyakaraj,  Rameswaram,

RAJYA SABHA [10 April, 2003]  
Tuticorin and Tiruchendur. Since the Centre is already working a viable inland 
waterways transport system, the Chennai- Kanyakumari waterways project can 
be explored on priority basis. Once this project is executed, even other places 
along the Coast of West Bengal, Orissa and Andhra Pradesh can be linked. 
Such a step will be a milestone in the economic development of the nation. 
This will also generate large scope for employment opportunities. Even small 
places with shallow water could be connected by using Jetties and Approach 
Boats. So, I appeal to the Centre to explore Chennai- Kanyakumari waterways 
transport project and execute it on a priority basis. Thank you.

Request to give highest priority to agriculture research and 
strengthening of ICAR and Agricultural Universities in the 
country 
SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN (Karnataka): Madam Deputy Chairman. 
I would like to draw, through you, the ki nd attention of the hon. Minister of 
Agriculture to my Special Mention pertaining to giving the highest priority for 
agriculture research and strengthening the Indian Council of Agriculture 
Research and the role of the agricultural universities in the country. 
The Indian average yield in rice and wheat ranks around 50 th in the 
world. The productivity growth in several commodities, especially food crops, 
is still unsteady and unstable. Henc e, there is a need to strengthen 
agricultural research system to respond to these challenges. Further, there is 
less investment in agriculture research.   To promote research of regional 
259 

RAJYA SABHA [10 April, 2003]  
importance and to aid better co-ordination of research in the region, the ICAR 
should set up a regional centre to oversee research in the region. In this 
context, Bangalore would be an ideal location for establishing a regional 
centre to cater to the needs of the Southern Region. 
Further, the University of Agricult ure Science, which has contributed 
a great deal for the success of the Green Revolution, is suffering for want of 
necessary facilities to match the needs of the day. Hitherto, the ICAR has laid 
more emphasis on research. It is, therefore, necessary that the ICAR would 
give equal important to agricultural ed ucation to produce quality manpower. In 
this endeavour, the ICAR should allocate more funds -- to the tune of 30 per 
cent -- to the agricultural education. 
It is also necessary that the adequate funding support from the ICAR 
may be provided for some of the burning  problems, which cut across the State 
boundaries, such as Mite in coconut and Yellow Leaf disease in areca, 
Nanjangud Rasabale, Coorg Mandrin and improving breed such as 
Amrithmahal, Bandur Sheep, Haliikar Animal Breed, etc., where present 
support is not at all adequate to tackl e the issue in a holistic manner. Thank 
you.

STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
Launch of INSAT - 3 A Satellite 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND THE DEPARTMENT OF SPACE 
(SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): Mada m, INSAT-3A satellite, India's 
state-of-the-art multi-mission mu lti purpose satellite for providing 
telecommunications, television, meteorological and search and rescue 
services was launched today at 04.22 1ST by Ariane-5 vehicle of Europe 
274 

[10 April. 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
from Kourou in French Guyana. It was separated from the launch vehicle at 
04.52 1ST and the signals were acquired at the INSAT Master Control Facility 
at Hassan, Karnataka. The satellite is  currently in the Geo-Synchronous 
Transfer Orbit of 36.055 km by 859 km with an inclination of 1.99 degrees with 
respect to the equator. The satellite is  now under the control of INSAT-MCF. 
Initial health checks from INSAT-MCF indi cate that all the subsystems of the 
satellite are performing nominally. 
The orbit of the satellite will be gradually raised to the Geo-
Synchronous Orbit (GSO) through a series of manoeuvres from INSAT-MCF 
over the next few days. After the satellite reaches the GSO, the solar array 
deployment, antenna deployment and the sail deployment will be performed. 
This will be followed by the checkout of the payload after which the satellite 
will be declared ready for operations. 
Today, the INSAT system is one of the largest domestic 
multipurpose satellite systems in the world with more than 85 communications 
transponders and payloads for meteorological applications. It provides a 
variety of services in the area of  telecommunications, TV broadcasting, 
developmental communication, education, telemedicine,  rural development, 
weather prediction and disaster warning. In this perspective, INSAT-3A 
represents the nation's resolve to use Space capabilities for a wide range of 
its developmental needs. 
Madam, through you, I would also like the House to join me in 
wishing the ISRO team all the best in the complex mission that is to be carried 
out in the next few days from the INSAT Master Control Facility at Hassan.
